q: The land of Mesopotamia lies mostly within which country today?
n: Mesopotamia, the land between the Tigris and Euphrates, is mostly modern Iraq.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - Mesopotamia

q: What material were Mesopotamian ziggurats built of?
n: Ziggurats used a sun-dried mud brick core, often faced with fired brick. Stone was scarce on the river plain.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - Mesopotamia, ziggurats

q: The Ziggurat of Ur was built under which civilization?
n: The Ziggurat of Ur was raised by the Sumerians under Ur-Nammu of the Third Dynasty of Ur.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - Sumerian architecture

q: What stone forms the bulk of the Great Pyramid at Giza?
n: The core and casing are limestone. Granite was kept for the chambers, portcullises and some casing details.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Ancient Egypt, the pyramids

q: Which triumphal arch in the Roman Forum commemorates the sack of Jerusalem in AD 70?
n: The Arch of Titus carries the relief of the spoils of the Temple. The Arc de Triomphe stands in Paris, so it is the usual distractor.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Roman triumphal arches

q: Which building has the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world?
n: The Pantheon's 43.3 m coffered dome is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome ever built.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Roman Pantheon

q: Which material let the Romans build vaults and domes at a scale the Greeks could not?
n: Roman concrete of lime, pozzolana and aggregate could be cast into vaults, domes and arches.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Roman construction

q: Which style is defined by the revival of classical symmetry, order and proportion?
n: The Renaissance revived the classical orders, symmetry and mathematical proportion. Baroque kept that language but broke its calm with movement and drama.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Italian Renaissance

q: Who designed One World Trade Center in New York?
n: David Childs of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill designed the tower. Libeskind did the site master plan.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - contemporary architecture

q: Who designed the Dancing House in Prague?
n: Frank Gehry designed it with the Czech architect Vlado Milunic.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - contemporary architecture

q: Who designed 30 St Mary Axe, the Gherkin, in London?
n: Norman Foster designed the tower, whose diagrid shell gives it its shape.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - contemporary architecture

q: Who designed the Lotus Temple in New Delhi?
n: The Iranian-Canadian architect Fariborz Sahba designed the nine-sided Baha'i House of Worship.
ref: Ching, Jarzombek and Prakash, A Global History of Architecture, 3rd ed. - contemporary architecture

q: Who designed the Parthenon in Athens?
n: Ictinus and Callicrates were the architects. Phidias directed the sculptural program.
ref: Fletcher, A History of Architecture, 20th ed. - Greek architecture, the Parthenon

q: Who designed the Philam Life Building on United Nations Avenue, Manila?
n: Carlos Arguelles designed the 1961 modernist building, known for the acoustics of its Philam Life Theater.
ref: Carlos Arguelles, Philam Life Building (1961) - Philippine modern architecture

q: Who designed the Philippine Heart Center in Quezon City?
n: Jorge Ramos designed the 1975 hospital in a Brutalist idiom. He also designed the GSIS headquarters in Pasay.
ref: Jorge Ramos, Philippine Heart Center (1975)

q: Who designed Santo Domingo Church in Quezon City?
n: Jose Maria Zaragoza designed the cruciform Art Deco church, completed in 1954.
ref: Jose Maria Zaragoza, Santo Domingo Church (1954)

q: Who said "Each new situation requires a new architecture"?
n: The line is Jean Nouvel's, who refuses a fixed personal style in favour of the specific situation.
ref: Jean Nouvel, Pritzker Prize lecture and collected interviews

q: Who said "Form and function are one"?
n: Wright recast his mentor Sullivan's "form ever follows function" into "form and function are one".
ref: Wright, An Autobiography; Sullivan, Lippincott's Magazine (1896)

q: Who said "Architecture is an expression of values"?
n: The line is Norman Foster's.
ref: Norman Foster, collected lectures and interviews

q: Who said "Even a brick wants to be something"?
n: Louis Kahn's teaching parable asks the brick what it wants to be, and the brick answers an arch.
ref: Kahn, Louis Kahn: Essential Texts

q: Who said architecture "should speak of its time and place, but yearn for timelessness"?
n: The line is Frank Gehry's.
ref: Frank Gehry, collected interviews

q: Who said his work is not about form follows function but "form follows beauty", or better, "form follows feminine"?
n: Oscar Niemeyer traced his curves to mountains, rivers and the female body rather than to function.
ref: Niemeyer, The Curves of Time

q: Who called architecture "the learned game, correct and magnificent, of forms assembled in the light"?
n: The line is Le Corbusier's, from Vers une architecture.
ref: Le Corbusier, Vers une architecture (1923)

q: Which term names the balanced arrangement of equivalent elements about a single median axis, so that only one plane divides the whole into identical halves?
n: Bilateral symmetry works about one axis. Radial symmetry arranges elements about a centre, so many planes can halve it.
ref: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space and Order, 4th ed. - Symmetry
